issues.title: related endpoints
issues.author: scburleigh
issues.body: In 1, "group of related endpoints" doesn't really mean anything, does it?  If we're not going to identify the nature of the relationship - that is, just how are these endpoints related? - then let's not try to say what the Group Number names.  If we are, then we should briefly explain it here.

issues.title: EID vs endpoint
issues.author: scburleigh
issues.body:
In 2., "in that imc EID" should be "in the endpoint identified by that imc EID".  Also "is therefore never a singleton endpoint" could be misread by an RFC 9171 novice as meaning "never contains just one bundle node."  That's not at all what it means, and of course it is not true, but to forestall confusion we might instead just say "is therefore not a singleton endpoint."

Also, it's not true that a group has no members of its own.  A group is a set of multicast endpoints, so its members are those multicast endpoints.  It's true that none of a group's members are BP nodes.

issues.title: 2-tuples?
issues.author: scburleigh
issues.body: 3.1  discusses cases "where an encoded imc URI does not explicitly include an Allocator Identifier" which seems to imply that an encoded imc URI that is a 2-tuple is valid; the Default Allocator is implicit.  But 3.2 says that there is no defined representation of an imc URI where the Allocator Identifier and Group Number are packed together as a single integer, which seems to be saying that no 2-tuple imc URI is valid.  Which is true?  Isn't an imc URI lacking an explicit Allocator Identifier (a 2-tuple) a Fully Qualified Group Number (FQGN)?

issues.title: zero group number
issues.author: scburleigh
issues.body: In 3.3.1, I think the second paragraph is not implied by the first, as stated.  According to the first paragraph, the imc URI "imc:91.0.5" seems to identify the Null imc URI, and so does the URI "imc:0.0.5" - and, for that matter, "imc:0.5" as well.  The second paragraph may be fine, except the words "This means that" need to be removed.

issues.title: utility of "groups"
issues.author: scburleigh
issues.body: Much of 5.1, particularly the fourth paragraph, seems somewhat vacuous.  Obviously implementations can do whatever they like; this will not be new information to an implementer.  Does it belong in an RFC?

issues.title: overreach
issues.author: scburleigh
issues.body: Isn't the purpose of this document simply to define the imc URI scheme?  Language in 5.2 (and 3.3, for that matter) imposes forwarding rules.  Doesn't the definition of those rules belong in the companion document on multicast forwarding that we agreed would be written?

issues.title: tautology
issues.author: scburleigh
issues.body: The last sentence of 5.2 is unnecessary.  It is not necessary to inform the reader that URIs formed in different schemes are different URIs.

issues.title: misplaced normative language
issues.author: scburleigh
issues.body: All of 5.3 derives directly from existing RFCs.  The observations provided in this section do spare the reader the agony of figuring this out, but it is informative; normative language is inappropriate.
